page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-3xL4 is an x86_64 architecture cloud server configured on the KVM hypervisor. This instance features 20 shared vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 12.8 GB per vCPU. The primary hardware highlight is the inclusion of three NVIDIA L4 graphics processing units based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined total of 72 GB of VRAM.

This server configuration does not include local storage, meaning block storage volumes must be attached separately for persistent data. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. A notable architectural tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce resource contention under sustained, non-GPU-bound computational loads compared to dedicated CPU instances.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high GPU and memory density, making it a specialized option for workloads that offload processing to the GPU rather than relying on dedicated CPU cores. The combination of 256.0 GB of RAM and 72 GB of total VRAM makes this instance type suitable for machine learning inference, data science pipelines, and GPU-accelerated rendering tasks that require substantial memory capacity but can tolerate shared CPU resources.
